Three birth times are in circulation for him. All three land on the same nakshatra — and its ruling planet is the strongest thing in his chart.

27 DEC 1965 · INDORE, MADHYA PRADESH

TL;DR

One nakshatra. Its lord, exalted.

Three different birth times circulate for Salman Khan, and they do not produce the same kundli. But every one of them puts his Moon in the same nakshatra — Dhanishta — and Dhanishta's ruling planet is Mars, which in this birth chart sits exalted in Capricorn: its single strongest sign.
So the planet that sets his entire dasha ladder is also the best-placed graha on the board. That is the one statement about his horoscope no birth-time argument can touch.

The other standout: Saturn in its own sign, Aquarius — and a Saturn mahadasha that ran for about nineteen years, covering the single most commercially dominant stretch of his career. Nothing in this chart is debilitated. Not one planet.

The decade the industry rebuilt around him

Maine Pyar Kiya released Dec 1989
  • He debuted in a supporting role in Biwi Ho To Aisi (1988), then led Maine Pyar Kiya (1989) — one of the biggest Hindi hits of its decade and the film that made him a household name.
  • Hum Aapke Hain Koun..! (1994) went on to become one of the highest-grossing Indian films ever made at that point, followed by Karan Arjun (1995) and Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999).
🔭 The Rahu → Jupiter handover lands somewhere between late 1986 and late 1988, depending on the birth time. His debut year sits right on that seam whichever one you take — and Jupiter is the growth-and-goodwill graha. A resonance, not a cause.

EARLY 00s–2010 · SATURN MAHADASHA OPENS

The slow years, then the reset

Being Human foundation launched 2007
  • The early 2000s were his least consistent commercial stretch in a decade — a run of films that underperformed against what came before.
  • In 2007 he set up the Being Human Foundation, which funds healthcare and education work and sells a clothing line whose proceeds go to the trust. It has since become as recognisable as most of his films.
  • Wanted (2009) reset the whole thing, and Dabangg (2010) turned the reset into a franchise.
🔭 Saturn's mahadasha opens somewhere between late 2002 and late 2004. Saturn is the graha of grind, delay and long structures — and it is sitting in Aquarius, a sign it owns.

  • He has hosted Bigg Boss from its fourth season in 2010 onward, which put him in Indian living rooms every week for months at a time, year after year.
  • On the film side, the Eid release slot effectively became his: Ek Tha Tiger (2012), Kick (2014), Bajrangi Bhaijaan (2015) and Sultan (2016) each set or approached box-office records on release.

The tea ☕

The three things people actually search

What the chart says about the pattern — and, just as often, what it honestly cannot say at all.

💍 "Why hasn't he married?"
What's public

He has never married. That's the whole of the public record, and it is the only part of it we're going to discuss — his private life is his own, and this page has nothing to say about who he has or hasn't been with.

What the chart can say

Genuinely: not much, and here's why. Marriage analysis in Vedic astrology is house work — the 7th house and its lord. Houses need the birth minute, and three different minutes are in circulation for him.

What holds by date alone: Venus in Capricorn (neutral by sign) and Jupiter retrograde in Gemini. Any site giving you a confident "marriage yog" verdict has quietly picked one of the three times and isn't telling you which.

🔥 The Eid-release streak
What's public

For most of the 2010s, an Eid weekend release from him was close to a guaranteed box-office event — Ek Tha Tiger, Kick, Bajrangi Bhaijaan, Sultan, Tiger Zinda Hai, one after another.

What the chart hints

All of it sits inside one long Saturn mahadasha, with Saturn in the sign it owns. Saturn's traditional signature isn't the lightning strike — it's the fixed slot, held for years, by repetition.

A streak is a very Saturn-shaped thing. That's an observation about a pattern, not a prediction about the next one.

💪 The physique, and the "bhai" persona
What's public

The shirtless entrance became a signature of his 2010s films, and his fitness has been a running part of his public image for over thirty years.

What the chart hints

Mars is the body graha — physical drive, muscle, appetite for confrontation. His Mars is exalted, the strongest dignity a planet gets.

It's also the lord of his birth nakshatra, Dhanishta, which traditional texts tie to stamina, rhythm and a kind of martial confidence. Same planet, showing up twice.

For the record — and kept out of the astrology

Two long-running legal matters are part of Salman Khan's public record. It would be dishonest to write a page about him and skip them, and equally dishonest to mention them without their outcomes. So, plainly:

  • The 2002 Mumbai hit-and-run case. A sessions court convicted him in May 2015. The Bombay High Court set that conviction aside and acquitted him of all charges in December 2015, holding the evidence insufficient. The Maharashtra government's appeal against that acquittal was admitted by the Supreme Court in July 2016 and remains pending. He stands acquitted.
  • The 1998 Kankani blackbuck case. A Jodhpur trial court convicted him in April 2018 and sentenced him to five years; he was granted bail two days later, and his appeal is pending before the Rajasthan High Court, which is still hearing it. Separately, the Rajasthan High Court acquitted him in two other poaching cases in 2016. A pending appeal is pending — not a conclusion.
And here is the line this site will not cross: nothing in this birth chart explains, predicts, causes or excuses any of the above. We do not read court outcomes out of planets, in either direction. Everything astrological on this page is about films, work and timing — nothing else.
Being straight with you: nobody outside someone's life knows why things really happen. Nothing above is a claim about what happened or why — it's a traditional reading of a publicly discussed birth chart, offered for entertainment. Facts are public record; the astrology is interpretation.
Certified comeback arcs

Two stretches that restarted a career

📉 → 🎬  The early-2000s dip, then Wanted

  • After a decade of era-defining hits, the early 2000s were his most inconsistent commercial run — enough that "past his peak" became a normal thing to write about him.
  • Wanted (2009) rewrote that verdict in a single weekend, and Dabangg (2010) made it a template other films copied for years.
  • He was 43 when Wanted released, and the decade that followed was the biggest of his career.

🔭 The chart bit: both films sit inside the long Saturn mahadasha — the graha most associated with results that arrive late, and only after the unglamorous part is done.

👕 → 🏥  A T-shirt line that became a hospital ward

  • The Being Human Foundation, launched in 2007, funds healthcare and education work; the clothing line under the same name channels proceeds to the trust.
  • It's one of the few Indian celebrity charities that turned into a self-funding consumer brand rather than a name on a letterhead.
  • Nearly two decades on, "Being Human" is recognised by people who couldn't name his last three films.

🔭 The chart bit: founded early in the Saturn era. Saturn is the karmic-duty graha in traditional readings — the one associated with service, obligation and slow-built institutions.

The question underneath most of these searches

A large share of the traffic that lands on pages like this one isn't really about the celebrity. It's someone checking whether their own janam kundli says what they've been told it says — usually about manglik dosha, or about matching two charts.

Vedic astrology has a whole 36-point guna Milan system built for exactly that second question, and it runs on both people's nakshatras. Ours computes it from birth data, not from vibes — and it will tell you when your own birth time isn't good enough to answer something, the same way this page does.

The manglik question specifically: it's a house question, so it needs your birth minute. If you have one, it's answerable in seconds. If you don't, an honest reading says so. How manglik dosha actually works →

Actually learn this

Astrology, but make it make sense

Zero background needed. Read this once and you can decode the birth chart above yourself — no astrologer required.

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

A kundli, or janam kundli, is a photo of the sky from the exact spot and second someone was born. Where each planet was sitting, frozen.

Vedic astrology treats that snapshot as the raw material a person was handed — not their fate, their starting kit.

His: his birthday is 27 December 1965, in Indore, Madhya Pradesh. That sky had the Sun in Sagittarius, Mars and Venus in Capricorn, Saturn in Aquarius, Jupiter retrograde in Gemini. Those placements do most of the talking on this page.
LESSON 02

The planets, and what each one does

Nine of them, or navagraha. Think of them as nine departments, each running one part of a life.

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it's comfortable and signs where it struggles. Same planet, different room, different output.

  • Exalted (strongest spot) — the planet is at maximum, working with the wind behind it.
  • Home ground (own sign) — the planet owns the place. Full strength, no permission needed.
  • Debilitated (weakest spot) — it's working with the handbrake on.
  • Everywhere else (neutral) — a guest. Functional, not special.
His scorecard is unusually clean: one planet exalted (Mars), one on home ground (Saturn), and nothing debilitated at all. Most charts carry at least one weak spot; his carries none. That's rarer than it sounds — and it says nothing about whether a life is easy, only about what the raw material looked like.
LESSON 04

Dashas — why timing is the whole game

This is the bit most people have never heard of, and it's the most useful.

Planets don't all act at once. They take turns running a life, for years at a stretch, in a fixed order the Moon's position sets at birth. Vedic astrology calls a planet's turn a dasha, and the full sequence for a lifetime is called the Vimshottari dasha.

His turns, in order:
Mars (from birth) → Rahu → Jupiter → Saturn → Mercury (current) → Ketu → Venus…

That order is fixed by his nakshatra and doesn't change no matter which of the three birth times you use. What does change is when each handover lands — by up to about two years. Which is why this page gives you eras and not anniversaries.
LESSON 05

Nakshatras — the 27 slices behind everything

Signs cut the sky into 12. Nakshatras cut it into 27, and Vedic astrology leans on them harder than on the signs for anything to do with timing.

Each nakshatra has a ruling planet. Whichever one the Moon occupies at birth decides which planet's mahadasha runs first — and therefore the order of every turn after it.

His is Dhanishta, ruled by Mars — traditionally symbolised by a drum, and associated with rhythm, stamina and a martial kind of confidence. The Moon spent all of 27 December 1965 inside it, which is why the dasha order on this page is solid even though the birth time isn't.
LESSON 06

Three birth times, and exactly what each one changes

This is the honest heart of the page, so here are the actual numbers rather than a shrug.

Three times circulate for 27 December 1965 in Indore: 10:45am (Astro-Databank, credited to Sy Scholfield citing the biography Being Salman), 2:30pm (AstroSage, and the value our own regression fixtures happen to carry), and 6:00am. Run all three:

Read the lagna row again. Scorpio, Aquarius, Aries — three completely different rising signs, which means three completely different house charts. That single row is why you will not find a house-based claim anywhere on this page, and why any site that gives you his "10th house of career" has silently picked one of the three.
LESSON 07

What we genuinely can't tell you

Here's where most celebrity astrology sites quietly cheat, and we won't.

A chart has two halves. Which sign each planet is in — that only needs the date, so everything above is solid. And the houses, which need the exact minute of birth, because the rising sign changes roughly every two hours.

The 10:45am time carries a strong source trail — a named biographer, a named nursing home. But a second time is published just as confidently by the largest astrology site in India, and a third floats around the databases. Rated is not the same as undisputed, and this site treats a live disagreement as a reason to publish less, not more.

So on this page you will not see us say "his career house" or "his 7th house of marriage". That would be a guess dressed as a fact. Other sites will. Ask them which birth time they used.
LESSON 08

So — is Salman Khan manglik?

One of the most-searched questions about him, and the honest answer is uncomfortable.

"Manglik" depends on which house Mars occupies — a specific short list of positions counted from the rising sign. Houses need the birth time. His rising sign comes out as Scorpio, Aquarius or Aries depending on which published time you take, which puts the very same Mars in three different houses.

What we can say honestly: his Mars is in Capricorn, where Mars is exalted — strong by sign, whatever house it lands in. Whether that counts as manglik depends entirely on a minute nobody has settled. Any site giving you a confident yes or no for him has picked a birth time and isn't telling you which.

Quick answers

What people ask about his kundli

FAQ 01

What is Salman Khan's birth time?

There isn't one settled answer. Three times circulate for 27 December 1965 in Indore: 10:45am, published by Astro-Databank with an A rating and credited to Sy Scholfield citing the biography Being Salman; 2:30pm, published on AstroSage's kundli page for him; and 6:00am, which turns up in other databases. They produce three different rising signs, so this page publishes only what all three agree on — planet signs, his nakshatra and his dasha eras — and never houses, lagna or a manglik verdict.

FAQ 02

What is Salman Khan's zodiac sign and nakshatra?

His birth nakshatra is Dhanishta, and that's certain — the Moon spent the entire day of 27 December 1965 inside it, so the birth-time dispute can't touch it. His Moon sign (rashi) is not settled: the Moon crosses from Capricorn into Aquarius at roughly 11:22am that day, so the 10:45am time gives Capricorn and the 2:30pm time gives Aquarius — which is exactly why you'll find both quoted online. By Vedic reckoning his Sun sign is Sagittarius; Western tropical astrology, which uses a different calculation, usually calls him a Capricorn.

FAQ 03

Is Salman Khan manglik?

This can't be answered honestly without a settled birth time, because manglik status depends on which house Mars occupies, not just its sign. His rising sign works out as Scorpio, Aquarius or Aries across the three published times — which puts the same Mars in three different houses and flips the answer with it. What is certain from the date alone: his Mars sits exalted in Capricorn, its strongest sign. Any source giving you a definite yes or no has assumed a birth time it isn't disclosing.

FAQ 04

Which mahadasha is Salman Khan running now?

The Mercury mahadasha — the seventeen-year turn that took over from a roughly nineteen-year Saturn mahadasha. The handover lands somewhere between late 2021 and late 2023 depending on which birth time you use, so we won't pin it to a date. The order itself is fixed by his Dhanishta nakshatra and is the same on all three charts: Mars, then Rahu, then Jupiter through the 1990s, then Saturn through the 2000s and 2010s, then Mercury now.

Method. Every placement, nakshatra and dasha sequence on this page is computed with the Swiss Ephemeris using the Lahiri ayanamsa — the same engine behind every AxtroShastra report — and was run at all three published birth times before anything was written. Because those three times produce three different rising signs, we publish only what the birth date and nakshatra settle (planet signs, nakshatras, dasha order) and deliberately avoid every house-based claim, including any manglik verdict and any marriage-timing verdict. Dasha handovers are given as eras because they move by up to about two years across the dispute.
